projectName: Group 9 Job Description & Resume Matching System
description: An academic NLP application that accepts real pasted or uploaded resumes and job descriptions, preprocesses text with NLTK, extracts contact information with regex, reports word frequency, computes TF-IDF and cosine similarity, supports an editable skill vocabulary, compares skills, and documents methodology and limitations.

services.name: Streamlit NLP application
services.features: Use actual pasted or uploaded resume and job description text with no fabricated results; provide NLTK preprocessing, regex contact extraction, word-frequency analysis, TF-IDF vectors, cosine similarity, editable skill vocabulary, skill comparison, tabs for the main workflow and documentation, and an Apple-inspired accessible visual system with restrained translucent materials, clear hierarchy, direct feedback, responsive layout, elegant typography, careful spacing, and reduced motion.

questions.question: Which language should power the Streamlit application?

options.label: Python
options.description: Use Python for Streamlit, NLTK preprocessing, and scikit-learn NLP calculations.

questions.rationale: The requested implementation is a Python Streamlit academic NLP project.

questions.question: Which framework should be used for the application interface and interaction flow?

options.label: Streamlit
options.description: Build the interactive single-page academic NLP tool in Python.

questions.rationale: The user explicitly requested a Streamlit system.

questions.question: Which workflow capabilities should the application include?
questions.answer: Accept pasted or uploaded resume and job description text; preprocess with NLTK; extract contact details with regex; show word frequency; compute TF-IDF and cosine similarity; allow editable skill vocabulary; compare matched and missing skills; include methodology and limitations tabs; never fabricate results.
questions.rationale: These are the functional requirements stated in the request.

questions.question: Which persistent data stores are required?

options.label: No datastore required
options.description: Process uploaded or pasted text in the active session without persistent storage.

options.label: PostgreSQL
options.description: Persist application records in a relational database.

options.label: Blob Storage
options.description: Persist uploaded files or other media.

questions.rationale: The requested academic tool can operate entirely on user-provided session data and should avoid storing resumes by default.

questions.question: Should users sign in for application API features?

options.label: No
options.description: Keep the academic demonstration accessible without accounts.

options.label: Yes
options.description: Require users to sign in before using application features.

questions.rationale: No authentication or user accounts were requested.

questions.question: What visual direction should guide the Streamlit interface?
questions.answer: Apple-inspired clarity and restraint: clear hierarchy, restrained translucent materials, direct feedback, responsive feel, elegant typography, careful spacing, reduced motion, and accessibility-conscious contrast and focus states.
questions.rationale: The user explicitly requested an Apple-inspired UI based on the supplied design principles.
